cases.sentence: Тяжело, с хрипом дышавший подли него один ___ и другой, скрипевший толстыми подошвами, мешали ему ясно слышать.
cases.translation: One nobleman breathing heavily with a wheeze beside him, and another creaking with thick soles, kept him from hearing clearly.
cases.explain: Дворянин is the grammatical subject of дышавший (breathing), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Толпа раздалась, чтобы дать дорогу подходившему к ___ Сергею Ивановичу.
cases.translation: The crowd parted to give way to Sergei Ivanovich, who was approaching the table.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case, giving столу.

cases.sentence: Он подошел к ___ и, ударив по нем перстнем, громко закричал.
cases.translation: He came up to the table and, striking it with his ring, shouted loudly.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case, giving столу.

cases.translation: Levin felt an unexpected sense of relief.
cases.explain: Чувство облегчения (a feeling of relief) requires the genitive case after the noun чувство, giving облегчения.

cases.sentence: Точно из смрадной ___ он вышел на чистый воздух.
cases.translation: It was as if he had walked out of a stuffy room into clean air.
cases.explain: The preposition из (out of) governs the genitive case, giving комнаты.

cases.sentence: Левин вошел в залу, получил беленький ___.
cases.translation: Levin went into the hall and received a little white ball.
cases.explain: Шарик is the direct object of the transitive verb получил (received), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.translation: Sergei Ivanovich placed his hand into the box.
cases.explain: Руку is the direct object of the transitive verb вложил (placed), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Он обратился к ___ с вопросом «Куда класть?».
cases.translation: He turned to Sergei Ivanovich with the question, "Where do I put it?"
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case, giving Сергею Ивановичу.

cases.translation: He had devoted 12 years of service to the nobility.
cases.explain: Двенадцать лет службы (twelve years of service) requires the genitive case after the quantity phrase, giving службы.

cases.sentence: В дверях губернский предводитель столкнулся с ___.
cases.translation: In the doorway the provincial marshal collided with Levin.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case, giving Левиным.

reading.question: Where was Levin standing during the debate?
reading.explain: The chapter opens by stating Levin stood rather far off.

reading.ru: В статье было сказано, что в случае разногласия надо баллотировать.
reading.question: What did the article of law say should happen in case of disagreement?
options: A new election should be called immediately
reading.explain: The text states the article said that in case of disagreement, a ballot must be held.

reading.ru: Но тут один высокий, толстый, сутуловатый, с крашенными усами, в узком мундире с подпиравшим ему сзади шею воротником помещик, перебил его.
reading.question: Who interrupted Sergei Ivanovich while he was explaining the article?
options: A tall, stout, stooped landowner with dyed mustaches
reading.correct: A tall, stout, stooped landowner with dyed mustaches
reading.explain: The text describes a tall, stout, stooping landowner with dyed mustaches interrupting him.

reading.ru: «Баллотировать! На шары нечего разговаривать! На шары!»
reading.question: What did the landowner shout out?
options: "Ballot! No need to talk, to the balls!"
reading.correct: "Ballot! No need to talk, to the balls!"
reading.explain: The text quotes the landowner shouting for balloting and to stop talking and go to the balls.

reading.ru: Левин совершенно не понимал, в чем было дело, и удивлялся той страстности, с которой разбирался вопрос о том, баллотировать или не баллотировать мнение о Флерове.
reading.question: What confused Levin about the debate?
options: He did not understand the matter and was amazed at the passion over whether to ballot on Flerov
He did not know who Flerov was at all
He thought the debate was about taxes
He was confused about the seating arrangement
reading.correct: He did not understand the matter and was amazed at the passion over whether to ballot on Flerov
reading.explain: The text says Levin completely failed to understand the matter and was astonished by the passion with which the question of balloting on the opinion about Flerov was debated.

reading.ru: Чтобы избавиться от этого тяжелого чувства, он, не дождавшись конца прений, ушел в залу, где никого не было, кроме лакеев около буфета.
reading.question: What did Levin do to escape his heavy feeling during the debate?
options: He left for a hall with only footmen near the buffet
He went outside for fresh air
He fell asleep in his chair
reading.correct: He left for a hall with only footmen near the buffet
reading.explain: The text says that to escape this oppressive feeling he left before the debate ended, going into a hall where there was no one but footmen by the buffet.

reading.question: How did Levin feel after leaving the tense debate for the quiet hall?
reading.explain: The text explicitly says Levin experienced an unexpected feeling of relief.

reading.ru: Ему очень понравилось, как один лакей с седыми бакенбардами, выказывая презрение к другим, молодым, которые над ним подтрунивали, учил их, как надо складывать салфетки.
reading.question: What did Levin enjoy watching among the footmen?
options: An old gray-whiskered footman teaching younger ones how to fold napkins
reading.correct: An old gray-whiskered footman teaching younger ones how to fold napkins
reading.explain: The text describes Levin's pleasure at watching an old footman with gray whiskers teach the younger ones how to fold napkins, showing contempt for their teasing.

reading.ru: Левин вошел в залу, получил беленький шарик и вслед за братом Сергеем Ивановичем подошел к столу
reading.question: What happened when Levin entered the hall for the vote?
options: He received a small white ball and followed his brother to the table
He was turned away at the door
He was asked to give a speech
reading.correct: He received a small white ball and followed his brother to the table
reading.explain: The text says Levin entered the hall, received a little white ball, and followed his brother Sergei Ivanovich to the table.

reading.ru: Сергей Иванович нахмурился. «Это дело убеждения каждого», — сказал он строго.
reading.question: How did Sergei Ivanovich react when Levin asked where to place his ball?
options: He frowned and said sternly that it was a matter of each person's own conviction
reading.correct: He frowned and said sternly that it was a matter of each person's own conviction
reading.explain: The text shows Sergei Ivanovich frowning and saying sternly that it was a matter of each person's own conviction.

reading.ru: «126 избирательных! 98 неизбирательных!» прозвучал невыговаривающий букву «Р» голос секретаря.
reading.question: What was the result announced by the secretary regarding the ballot on Flerov?
reading.explain: The text quotes the secretary's announcement of 126 electable and 98 non-electable votes.

reading.ru: Отвечая дворянам, Снедков говорил о доверии дворянства, о любви к нему, которой он не стоит, ибо вся заслуга его состоит в преданности дворянству, которому он посвятил 12 лет службы.
reading.question: What did Snetkov say in his emotional response to the nobles?
options: That he did not deserve their trust and love, having only devoted 12 years of service
That he was resigning immediately in anger
That the nobility should abolish the marshal's post
That he planned to run again next year regardless
reading.correct: That he did not deserve their trust and love, having only devoted 12 years of service
reading.explain: The text has Snetkov say he did not deserve the nobility's trust and love, as his only merit was his devotion in 12 years of service.

reading.ru: Большинство дворян было тронуто, и Левин почувствовал нежность к Снедкову.
reading.question: How did most of the nobles, and Levin, react to Snetkov's emotional speech?
options: They were moved, and Levin felt tenderness toward Snetkov
They booed him off the stage
reading.correct: They were moved, and Levin felt tenderness toward Snetkov
reading.explain: The text states the majority of the nobles were touched, and Levin felt tenderness toward Snetkov.

reading.ru: «Я устал, уж стар. Есть достойнее и моложе меня. Пусть послужат».
reading.question: What did the marshal say when Levin asked if he was again their marshal?
options: That he was tired and old, and younger, worthier men should serve
That he was thrilled to continue serving
That he planned to challenge the results
That he wanted to appoint his son instead
reading.correct: That he was tired and old, and younger, worthier men should serve
reading.explain: The text quotes the marshal saying he was tired, already old, and that there were worthier and younger men who should serve.

reading.ru: Узнав об этом, новая партия успела во время прений о Флерове послать на извозчики своих обмундировать дворянина и из двух напоенных привезти одного в собрание.
reading.question: What did the new party do upon learning that the old party had gotten two noblemen drunk and stolen a third's uniform?
options: They sent cabs to get a nobleman properly dressed and bring one of the drunk men to the assembly
They reported the old party to the governor
They gave up and withdrew their candidate
reading.correct: They sent cabs to get a nobleman properly dressed and bring one of the drunk men to the assembly
reading.explain: The text says that upon learning of this, the new party managed, during the Flerov debate, to send cabs to get a nobleman properly uniformed and bring one of the two drunk men to the assembly.
